1.explanation: The file src/languages/powershell.js defines the grammar and regular expressions used to detect and highlight PowerShell parameters. Its current option‐matching pattern only accounts for a single leading dash and ignores the double‐dash form. Therefore, updating this file’s regex or mode for parameters to accept `--` prefixes will resolve the missing highlight for double flags.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting PowerShell code, single‐dash parameters (e.g. -Flag) are recognized and highlighted correctly, but double‐dash parameters (e.g. --Flag) are not. The sample shows “foo --bar baz” rendered as plain text while “foo -bar baz” is tokenized. In contrast, PowerShell Core’s native console highlights both single‐ and double‐dash flags.

2.explanation: The file powershell.js defines the grammar rules and regex patterns for PowerShell in highlight.js. In it, the parameter (flag) rule currently matches only a single leading dash (e.g. /^-[A-Za-z]+/). To support double hyphens, you need to adjust the regex or add an alternative pattern (e.g. /--[A-Za-z]+/) so that --flags are also captured under the same "meta" class and receive the correct highlighting.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting PowerShell code, single‐dash parameters (e.g. -Bar) are correctly given the “meta” (parameter) style, but double‐dash parameters (e.g. --Bar) are not recognized at all. In the screenshot you can see “-bar” highlighted, but “--bar” left as plain text. PowerShell Core itself treats both forms as valid parameters, so highlight.js’s PowerShell highlighter needs to be updated to match “--” prefixes too.
